item.title: Democrats' Latest Rising Star Has Unfinished Business in Georgia
item.description: Speculation is swirling around Senator Jon Ossoff’s presidential ambitions — but first he needs to win reelection, help win the governorship, and keep peace with his fellow Georgia senator. Josh Wingrove expalins. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: McBurney: US Iran Military Action Unlikely Near Midterms
item.description: Oil rose on signs the US might resume military action against Iran following repeated threats from President Trump. Meanwhile Saudi Arabia has intercepted Houthi missiles and drones in Riyadh & Mecca region. Niamh McBurney, Director at Control Risks spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on the escalation in the region. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China-Hawk Philippine Defense Chief Open to Presidential Bid
item.description: Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said he’s open to a presidential run in 2028, potentially pitting the China hawk against current Vice President Sara Duterte.
item.dc:creator: Andreo Calonzo and Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: Healey’s Tax Break for Startups Branded a Turkey That Will Fail
item.description: John Healey’s new tax break for company founders will fail to meet the Chancellor of the Exchequer’s goal of keeping ambitious and successful entrepreneurs in the UK, economists and tax experts said.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White and Katia Porzecanski

item.title: Modi’s Mass Detentions Stoke Anger Among Young India Protesters
item.description: When Indian police closed in on young protesters in New Delhi this month, Simran locked hands with a friend. They made a quick pact: if they were getting hauled away, they were going together.
item.dc:creator: Asmi Bhatia

item.title: UK Firms Open Up Offices to Let Trade Unions Recruit Members
item.description: British businesses now have to let trade union members into their offices to recruit after the Labour government’s overhaul of workers’ rights.
item.dc:creator: Irina Anghel

item.title: Daron Acemoglu Has a Warning for Democrats
item.description: Nobel laureate Daron Acemoglu on why he believes liberals have failed the working class, the case against social media algorithms and that Economist article. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Two Nordic Leaders Defied Russia Hawks With Putin Outreach
item.description: Alexander Stubb and Jonas Gahr Støre are parlaying a two-decade friendship into diplomatic power.
item.dc:creator: Kirsi Heikel, Heidi Taksdal Skjeseth and Ott Ummelas

item.title: Johannesburg Risks a ‘Total Collapse’ of Its Water Network
item.description: South Africa’s water shortages are acute in the country’s economic center, where there’s a gaping divide between those who can afford emergency fixes and those who can’t. It’s a big issue in next week’s local elections.
item.dc:creator: S'thembile Cele and Bonolo Mokonoto

item.title: Thailand Probes Assets of Chief Rabbi Stripped of Citizenship
item.description: Thai authorities are examining the landholdings and businesses of the country’s chief rabbi after Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stripped him of Thai citizenship, widening scrutiny of a religious leader who has lived in the country for more than three decades.
item.dc:creator: Erich Parpart

item.title: Trump Cancels Rallies, Switches to Remote Midterm Campaigning
item.description: President Donald Trump canceled appearances in Kansas and Iowa for the closing days of the midterm election season, and will instead hold “a large number of tele-rallies,” the Republican National Committee announced on Thursday evening.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Erik Wasson

item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Sen. Rick Scott (R-FL) says the US should “demolish” Iran’s regime and argues the country must prepare for war to achieve peace and prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. Patrick McHenry, former House Financial Services Committee chair and Bloomberg contributor, says Democrats are likely to win control of the House, though the size of their majority remains uncertain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Debrief: How Democratic Control Could Reshuffle Congress' Most Powerful Committees
item.description: Bloomberg’s Mario Parker joined the show to discuss how Democratic control of Congress could reshape oversight of Wall Street, AI and cryptocurrency. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan Government to Scale Back Gasoline Subsidies From December
item.description: Japan plans to gradually scale back gasoline subsidies from December into early spring, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said, adding that support for electricity and gas bills, which was also provided from January through March this year, will be brought forward and begin in December.
item.dc:creator: Akemi Terukina

item.title: Trump on Alaska Sen. Race Controversy: It's Voter Fraud
item.description: Bloomberg’s Anna Edgerton joined the show to discuss the Alaska Senate race and the potential legal and campaign-finance questions surrounding ballot stacking. She speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: McHenry Sees Democratic House, GOP Leadership Fight
item.description: Patrick McHenry, former House Financial Services Committee chair and Bloomberg contributor, says Democrats are likely to win control of the House, though the size of their majority remains uncertain. McHenry says a Republican loss could set up a leadership battle between Jim Jordan and Steve Scalise, with Scalise’s existing leadership infrastructure potentially giving him an advantage. McHenry says Hakeem Jeffries could face a difficult task managing Democrats even if he becomes speaker, particularly with a narrow majority and ideological divisions inside the caucus. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Scott Says US Should ‘Demolish’ Iran’s Regime
item.description: Sen. Scott (R-FL) says the US should “demolish” Iran’s regime and argues the country must prepare for war to achieve peace and prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. Sen. Scott says the US military has the capability to bring the conflict to a conclusion rather than continue costly operations protecting oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Sen. Scott says he opposes government grants to companies but would prefer taxpayers receive equity when federal money is provided, arguing the government should seek a return on those investments. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Businessweek Daily: Amazon Chip Earnings (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Amazon reported higher capital spending than expected, while its e-commerce revenue slowed ahead of a potentially lukewarm holiday sales season. Intel's revenue forecast missed estimates, hurt by sputtering demand for PC processors and supply-chain problems with its lucrative data center companies.
On today's episode:
Kunjan Sobhani, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Semiconductor Analyst Anurag Rana, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Tech Analyst Jake Silverman, Bloomberg Intelligence Semiconductor Analyst Liz Ann Sonders, Schwab Chief Investment Strategist Mike Townsend, Schwab Managing Director of Legislative & Regulatory Affairs (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fox News Moves South Carolina Senate Contest to Toss-Up in New Rating
item.description: President Donald Trump returned to South Carolina on Thursday to bolster incumbent Senator Darline Graham, as her race in the historic Republican stronghold was moved to a “toss-up” by Fox News.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson and Skylar Woodhouse

item.title: China Elevates Key Figure in Purges With Rare Politburo Pick
item.description: The Chinese Communist Party restocked its powerful Politburo for the first time in more than three decades and announced plans to hold a congress next year, where it’s set to unveil new leadership.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
